sources.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches tomorrow, November 19
sources.text: The latest installment in the Grand Theft Auto series heads to the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond. Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive. Grand Theft Auto VI arrives on PlayStation 5 Thursday, November 19, available at PlayStation Store. The game is set in the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond in the biggest, most immersive evolution of the series yet. Jason grew up around grifters and crooks. After a stint in the Army trying to shake off his troubled teens, he found himself in the Keys doing what he knows best, working for local drug runners. Meeting Lucia could be the best or worst thing to ever happen to him. Jason knows how he’d like it to turn out but right now, it’s hard to tell. Lucia’s father taught her to fight as soon as she could walk, and life has been coming at her swinging ever since. Fighting for her family landed her in the Leonida Penitentiary. Sheer luck got her out but now more than anything, Lucia wants the good life her mom has dreamed of since their days in Liberty City. Instead of half-baked fantasies, Lucia is prepared to take matters into her own hands. Leonida is made up of six regions: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga. Here’s a closer look at what makes each region unique. The glamour, hustle, and greed of America captured in a single city. Each neighborhood has something to offer, from the pastel art deco hotels and bright white sands of Ocean Beach, to the bustling panaderías of Little Cuba and the bootleg brands of the Tisha-Wocka flea market, out to the VC Port, the cruise ship capital of the world. We’re a long way from the ’80s, but Vice City is still the sun and fun capital of America Life in this tropical archipelago isn’t flashy but it’s easy. Get your buzz on and pull up a deck chair but look out — you are right on the doorstep of some of the most beautiful and dangerous waters in all of America. You never know what lies beneath the surface of this primordial expanse. The gators may be the most famous attraction, but there are far deadlier predators and weirder discoveries among the mangroves. Cheap motels, shut-down attractions, and empty strip malls won’t bring the tourists back, but there’s a new economy in this once-popular vacation spot. It’s fueled by malt liquor, painkillers, and truck stop energy drinks. In the heart of Leonida, American industry and old school values still reign supreme — whatever the cost. The Allied Crystal sugar refinery provides the jobs, while the local biker gang provides almost everything else. A national landmark up against the state’s northern border, Mount Kalaga offers prime hunting, fishing, and off-road trails. In the lush surrounding backwoods, hillbilly mystics and paranoid radicals live far from the prying eyes of the government. Spanning stations including Classic Rock, Modern Hip-Hop, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latin, ‘80s, Electronic, Blues, Ballads, Talk Radio, and much more, Grand Theft Auto VI features the biggest and widest-ranging selection of in-game radio yet. Plus, for the first time ever, Grand Theft Auto VI introduces a series of on-demand podcasts for Jason and Lucia to experience beyond Leonida’s terrestrial radio, with both radio and podcasts available to listen to in vehicles and on foot through newly introduced headphones and earbuds connected to their smartphones.

sources.title: Grand Theft Auto VI chega amanhã, dia 19 de novembro
sources.text: O mais novo título da série Grand Theft Auto nos leva ao estado de Leonida, até as ruas iluminadas de neon de Vice City e além. Jason e Lucia sempre souberam que as cartas não estavam a favor deles. Mas quando o que deveria ser um trabalho fácil dá errado, eles se encontram no lado mais escuro do lugar mais ensolarado da América, no meio de uma conspiração criminosa que cobre todo o estado de Leonida, forçados a depender um do outro mais do que nunca se quiserem sair vivos. Grand Theft Auto VI chega para PlayStation 5 quinta-feira, 19 de novembro, disponível na PlayStation Store. O jogo se passa no estado de Leonida, onde ficam as ruas banhadas de neon de Vice City e além, na maior e mais imersiva evolução da série até hoje. Jason cresceu rodeado de bandidos e vigaristas. Após um período no exército para tentar se livrar de sua adolescência perturbada, ele se encontra nos Keys fazendo o que faz melhor, trabalhando para traficantes de drogas locais. Conhecer Lucia pode ser a melhor ou a pior coisa que já aconteceu com ele. Jason sabe como gostaria que tudo terminasse, mas agora, é difícil prever. O pai de Lucia a ensinou a lutar desde que ela aprendeu a andar, e a vida tem vindo com tudo para cima dela desde então. Lutar por sua família a colocou na Penitenciária de Leonida. Sorte pura a livrou desta vez, mas agora mais do que qualquer coisa, Lucia deseja a vida boa com a qual sua mãe sonhava desde que moravam em Liberty City. Em vez de fantasias pela metade, Lucia está preparada para assumir o controle da situação. Leonida é composto de seis regiões: Vice City, as Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, e Mount Kalaga. Vamos conhecer o que torna cada região única. O glamour, o trabalho e a ganância da América capturados em uma única cidade. Cada bairro tem algo a oferecer, dos hóteis de art deco, cores pastel e areia branca de Ocean Beach, até as padarias de Little Cuba e as marcas falsificadas do mercadinho de Tisha-Wocka, até o VC Port, a capital mundial dos navios de cruzeiro. Estamos longe dos anos 80, mas Vice City ainda é a capital do sol e da diversão da América. A vida neste arquipélago tropical não é chamativa, mas é boa. Pegue uma cervejinha e puxe uma cadeira de praia, mas tome cuidado, você está à beira das águas mais belas e perigosas da América. Você nunca sabe o que está sob a superfície desta região primordial. Os jacarés podem ser a atração mais famosa, mas há predadores bem mais perigosos e descobertas mais estranhas entre o manguezal. Motéis baratos, atrações fechadas, e galerias de lojas vazias e abandonadas não vão trazer os turistas de volta, mas há uma nova economia neste local que já foi um ponto turístico. Agora mandam o as bebidas baratas, remédios contra a dor e bebidas energéticas. No coração de Leonida, a indústria Americana e os antigos valores ainda reinam supremos, seja qual for o custo. A refinaria de açúcar Allied Crystal providencia os empregos, e a gangue de motociclistas local providencia quase todo o resto. Um marco nacional na fronteira norte do estado, Mount Kalaga oferece as melhores trilhas off-road e pontos de pesca e caça. Nas florestas em torno, caipiras místicos e radicais paranóicos vivem longe dos olhos vigilantes do governo. Com estações de Rock Clássico, Hip-Hop Moderno, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latina, Anos 80, Electrônica, Blues, Baladas, Talk Radio, e muito mais, Grand Theft Auto VI possui a maior e mais variada seleção de rádios em um jogo até hoje. Além disso, pela primeira vez, Grand Theft Auto VI apresenta uma série de podcasts sob demanda para Jason e Lucia ouvirem além das rádios de Leonida, com ambos disponíveis para ouvir em veículos e a pé usando fones de ouvido e earbuds conectados aos seus smartphones.

sources.title: What Console Should You Buy for GTA 6? We Break Down PS5 vs. Xbox Pricing, Deals, and More
sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here. After years of trailers, delays, rumours, and more leaks than Rockstar Games would probably care to count , we can finally get our hands on one of the most anticipated games of all time. GTA 6 is now available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S , having officially launched on November 19, 2026. And while plenty of players will already have their consoles hooked up and ready to go, there are still some pretty important questions worth asking: which console actually offers the best way to play GTA 6? Is it worth upgrading to a PS5 Pro? And should you even buy a console for it, or simply wait for the inevitable PC release instead ? Look, there's no doubt that the vast majority of players will end up playing GTA 6 on PS5 . Sony's console has a sizeable lead over Xbox Series X|S, with around 95 million PS5 consoles sold , compared with an estimated 35 million Xbox Series X|S consoles . But it's not quite as simple as saying, "play it on PS5, like everyone else." For starters, plenty of people still haven't made the jump to the current generation. If you're still playing on PS4 or Xbox One, GTA 6 could well be the game that finally convinces you to upgrade. Unfortunately, you couldn't have picked a much more expensive time to do it, with console prices, games, storage, and just about everything else seemingly getting pricier by the minute. It's a sign of the times, I'm afraid. Then there's the question of performance. Rockstar's latest open-world adventure is an enormously ambitious game, and the standard PS5 and Xbox Series X|S have their work cut out for them. The PS5 Pro, meanwhile, has considerably more horsepower than the standard PS5, along with PSSR upscaling, making it an interesting option for anyone looking to get the best possible experience. The PS5 Pro is certainly the console I'd be looking at if money were no object. It has a more powerful GPU than the standard PS5, improved ray tracing capabilities, and Sony's PSSR upscaling technology, all of which should help it get more out of demanding games. That doesn't automatically make it a worthwhile upgrade, though. I'd be wary of spending hundreds of dollars extra on a PS5 Pro purely for the promise of better performance in GTA 6 . There's a difference between getting a sharper image or more consistent performance and suddenly unlocking a completely different experience. Whether those improvements justify the considerable price premium is another matter entirely. That being said, if you forced me to give an answer, the PS5 Pro is still probably the best option for getting the most out of GTA 6 on console. If only it wasn't so horrendously expensive, and so difficult to find at a reasonable price right now. If you don't already own a PS5 or Xbox Series X|S , GTA 6 presents a slightly awkward conundrum. On the one hand, this is arguably the biggest game release of the generation ( and probably of all time, quite honestly ), and you're probably going to want to play it ASAP. On the other, buying an entire console for one game is an increasingly expensive proposition in 2026. Sony's current US prices put the PS5 Digital Edition at $599.99 , the standard PS5 with a disc drive at $649.99 , and the PS5 Pro at a frankly eye-watering $899.99 . Microsoft isn't doing much better, with the Xbox Series S now costing $499.99 and the Xbox Series X reaching $749.99 for the digital model or $799.99 with a disc drive. Yikes. Yet, somehow, despite these bonkers prices, there's somehow also an argument for buying sooner rather than later. Console prices have been consistently heading in the wrong direction, and the broader component shortage isn't exactly helping. Major retailers have already warned that console stock could struggle to keep up with demand over the holiday period, with one senior games buyer claiming retailers have been told they won't receive the number of consoles they want ahead of GTA 6's launch. That's not exactly a guarantee that you'll be fighting scalpers for a PS5 come November, though. Sony insists it has secured enough memory to hit its PS5 sales target for the financial year, despite the ongoing component difficulties. Yet, with GTA 6 expected to drive a huge upgrade cycle, I'd rather have my console sorted well before November 19 than find myself scrambling for one at the last minute. Still, if you can, I would still avoid rushing out and paying full price for a console simply because GTA 6 is coming. If you're starting from scratch, keep an eye out for bundles, retailer promotions, trade-in offers, and, particularly as we get closer to November, any GTA 6-specific console deals that might appear. Honestly, refurbished is where I'd be looking right now if you're trying to keep the cost of getting GTA 6-ready as low as possible. You're not going to get much of a discount on brand-new PS5 hardware at the moment, so a reputable refurbished model can make considerably more sense. That's why the next deal I'd consider is a certified refurbished PS5 directly from PlayStation through the PS Direct store . A refurbished PS5 is currently $549, while the refurbished PS5 Digital Edition is $499. If you're happy with digital games, the $499 refurbished PS5 Digital Edition is arguably the most compelling option of the lot, particularly if GTA 6 is the main reason you're buying a console in the first place . ICYMI: Sony has also announced plans to stop producing physical game discs for new PlayStation releases from January 2028, meaning we're potentially looking at the final few years of physical PlayStation gaming. That doesn't mean your existing discs suddenly become useless, or that physical games are disappearing overnight, but it does make the $50 saving on a Digital Edition a little more tempting if you're starting from scratch and don't have an existing physical library. sources.title: Should you kill or spare Arnold in GTA 6?
sources.text: Deciding whether to kill or spare Arnold in GTA 6 is the culmination of the Hey Arnold mission in Chapter 1, the 7th after you encounter Mandy during Pipework. Essentially, Arnold, Brian's business partner, has gone dark, so you're sent to rough him up. Arnold and his cronies will do a runner, hopping into a vehicle and speeding off. You'll need to chase them down and do a bit of high-speed shooting. This will lead to an on-foot chase, at the end of which you'll corner him on a pier, where he'll explain he wants to leave the criminal life behind and disappear. There are two choices and consequences: Funnily enough, if you choose neither and just wait, Arnold will leave, though this will result in the same outcome as if you decided to spare him. Besides this, there are no downsides to sparing him or advantages gained through killing him. sources.title: Should you give the statue to Benedict Halifax in GTA 6?
sources.text: In the Chapter 3 mission Dubious Provenance, should you trust, or not trust, the eccentric antiques dealer? Deciding whether to give the statue to Benedict Halifax is a decision you'll need to make during the fourth story mission of Chapter 3 in GTA 6 , called Dubious Provenance. This mission will kick off after Cal visits the Bayside apartment you're borrowing from Boobie to inspect the hard drive. Once Cal leaves, you'll see an icon of a statuette at the closet door. Remember, you didn't just acquire a hard drive but a bronze statuette in Chapter 1, and if you interact with it now the mission will begin. First, you need to drive to Capri, a ritzy town on the other side of the map. At the antiques store, Evelyn Andrews tells you she isn't interested in the obviously stolen item, but art dealer Benedict Halifax approaches you on the sly and says he can have it appraised for you. Should you give the statue to him? So, you might as well just give it to him. Things shake out the same way no matter what you choose, but not giving it to him just means the mission will ultimately take longer to complete. sources.title: Should you spare or kill Arnold for 'Hey Arnold' in GTA 6?
sources.text: Arnold's not having a good day, no matter how you slice it Arnold's not having a good day, no matter how you slice it Deciding whether to spare or kill Arnold in Grand Theft Auto 6 's "Hey Arnold" quest is one of your first big branching decisions in the game. It seems like a big one, though while it will influence certain aspects of your playthrough, it doesn't dramatically alter how the story unfolds. Brian doesn't even care how you get the job done. He just wants to know it's done so he can carry on with his job. Below, we explain whether you should spare or kill Arnold in GTA 6 's "Hey Arnold" quest and what happens for both choices. After Jason and Brian catch up with Arnold and his minions fall by the wayside, Jason leaves the truck, and you'll chase Arnold on foot for a bit. Arnold corners himself at the end of a small personal pier behind a house, and there's no chance of losing him this time. Arnold drops to his knees and starts begging once you catch up, claiming he just wants out of the whole horrible business and really doesn't care what happens to Brian or their mutual clients. He promises to slip away quietly and never come back if you spare him, though, of course, you're the one with the final decision to make. That's assuming you made it to this point. If you catch up with Arnold while driving Brian's truck before Arnold legs it, you can force this encounter earlier or just run him over. Anyway, if you do chase Arnold to the end of the metaphorical road, after he says you can take the scraps and asks again for you not to kill him, press L2/LT to focus on him . Jason automatically draws whatever weapon you have equipped and points it at Arnold, but if you press X on PlayStation 5 or A on Xbox, you can spare Arnold . If you don't want to spare him, fire the weapon to finish the job. If you kill Arnold in any way, either with a headshot or by running him over, Jason gets a boost in his status as a violent criminal. If you spare Arnold , Jason gets a "restrained" bonus that goes toward his status as a professional, non-violent criminal. You can also beat him up or shoot him in the body to get a "ruthless" stat boost, a beige face icon with horns — not the purple devil that accompanies violent actions, but not a boost to professionalism, either. This one choice won't be enough to fully change your criminal profile , as you can still change Jason's (and Lucia's) behavior as you progress through the game, but if you're aiming for a violent or non-lethal playstyle, it's best to just pick the action that aligns with those goals. Or if you want cash, you should spare Arnold too. After time passes, Arnold sends Jason some cash for sparing his life — $10,000 . This didn't happen until roughly Chapter 4 for us, though the way some story elements happen out of order in GTA 6 depending on your actions, the timing might be different for you. You get the notification via text message from Brian, so you'll know when the money's ready for you to collect. If you're just getting started in GTA 6 , we've got plenty of guides to help you live the high life in Leonida. Check out our GTA 6 beginner guide to get a grasp of the basics and our tips for what to do first , recommendations for the best ways to make money fast , and explainer for how to keep stolen weapons and cars to make the most of your free time. Our selection of GTA 6 guides includes help for things like how to steal the Phoenix in "Unwanted Attention" and whether you should defuse Mandy , too. There's a set of explainers for GTA 6 's more open-ended side activities, like how to rob the Exotic Animal Front and where to find tree effigies for the Skunk Ape mission , and we've got all the GTA 6 cheat codes . You'll have to put in some effort before you can use those, though.

sources.title: How to Get Ready for November 19
sources.text: November 19, 2026, has long been circled on your calendar. Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your XBOX console. We can hardly believe it’s almost here, either. Once midnight strikes, you want to be locked in the action, so to help you prepare, we created a checklist to ensure distractions are put to bed so you can settle in for a season of gaming like nothing you’ve ever experienced before. 2026 has been full of some absolute bangers: Gears of War E-Day, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Forza Horizon 6, Halo: Campaign Evolved, Minecraft Dungeons II, Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred , Control Resonant , Mixtape , Pragmata , The Blood of Dawnwalker , Star Wars: Galactic Racer , 007 First Light , Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve … seriously, all these games came out this year . That also means you might have a hard drive that is nearing capacity. And you will be faced with some hard choices to free up approximately 212GB of space on your XBOX Series X|S before November 19. You could always upgrade the capacity of your console to keep all your games at the ready, using the storage expansion slot on the back of the console. Otherwise, you’ll have a hard choice to make which we do not envy. But know that you’re in good company – we had to find a way to make room too. XBOX Cloud Gaming means that you don’t need to own an XBOX Series X|S console to experience the latest games (or use up that hard drive space) – you can stream directly from the cloud to your XBOX One console. Game Pass subscribers receive an allotment of hours per month as part of their plans, but you can also purchase blocks of time . Certain upcoming major releases have been confirmed as cloud-ready on day one , so even if you don’t own a current gen console, your latest obsession isn’t out of reach. You never want to settle in for a long gaming session only to immediately get hit with an update download. If you haven’t used your XBOX Series X|S or XBOX One in a minute, be sure to power up and connect to the internet beforehand and make sure you’re all set with the latest system updates. You can also install any upcoming releases you may have pre-ordered, while you’re at it. If you’re feeling a gaming flu coming on (and there’s a lot of that going around right now), then take a sick day, rather than risk infecting your coworkers or classmates. Sometimes you just need to listen to your body’s needs, relax, and let the fever run its course. Miami’s own DJ Khaled, aka Dr. XBOX will write you a personalized note to help explain the situation. If this thing is really serious, you may even need the whole week to recover – it’s the responsible thing to do. We all have responsibilities. Some of them come with four legs and a suspect bladder. Don’t let Rufus ruin your gaming fun. Get ahold of a local dog walker to take them outside so you can enjoy the big day uninterrupted. Or drop them off at doggie daycare for a day (or week) to get them out of your hair. Is your XBOX in an area of the house that is easily accessible to younger players? Consider the steps you need to take to get it out of younger sightlines, like running an extension cable out to the shed in the backyard or huddling up in your at-home office. Even if you do find yourself bouncing between rooms, your save files reside in the Cloud, allowing you to pick up your session wherever you last plugged your console in. We’re always on the hunt for new tunes and one of the things we’re most looking forward to on November 19 is discovering a whole bunch of new tracks that are sure to make our listening playlist pop throughout the year. You can get started here on Spotify . XBOX Design Lab lets you create your own next-gen XBOX Wireless Controller. Choose from a combination of colors, patterns, textured grips, and more. You could even pick up some specially themed versions of controllers styled in hot pink and pastels – this one is particularly striking . Speaking of controllers, if you expect long gaming sessions in your near future, make sure that it’s plugged in so it has a full charge when you need it, or stock up on AA batteries. Maybe even get a backup controller ready so you can hot-swap them in and minimize interruptions. Looking for something to add to your queue? Check out the 1967 classic, “Bonnie and Clyde,” featuring Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway to get you in the mood for an epic story about two tragic lovers who fall into a life of crime. We’ll have to wait and see if the outcome is any different this time around starting on November 19.

sources.title: How to get Paul Walker's Fast and Furious car in GTA 6
sources.text: Get your hands on the classic bright green Fast and Furious Mitsubishi Eclipse in GTA 6 Finding, buying, and stealing your dream car or bike is a peak part of Grand Theft Auto, and mine is the Fast and Furious Mitsubishi Eclipse in GTA 6, based on the bright green car driven by Paul Walker as Brian O'Conner in the original movie. This gorgeous motor can be found locked in a garage in Vice City in GTA 6 , but it can be stolen, and, if you play your cards right, you can even register it as your own for free. Here's how. To find Paul Walker's Fast and Furious Mitsubishi in GTA 6, you need to head towards Vice Beach, to the east of Vice City. The car is locked in a garage on Vespucci Island, one of the Rialto Islands to the west of Vice Beach. You can see the exact location marked on the map above. You'll have to break into the garage and steal the car, which is actually a lot easier than it sounds, but I've got more details on that below. As you'd expect, the Mitsubishi handles really well and hits high speeds, so it's one of the best GTA 6 cars you can get your hands on, especially in the early game, for free, and without picking up too much heat. To steal Paul Walker's GTA 6 car, head to the garage and break in. This triggers an alarm, but you can switch that off pretty quickly on the wall to your left as you head in. Open the garage door here too, break into the car, hotwire it, and drive away - simple as that. There are a few additional details to note here, though, that make this experience easier or better for you overall. For more on car ownership in GTA 6, which can be done at any Pay 'n' Spray for a cost, check out our guide to GTA 6 personal vehicles . sources.title: How To Get A Bank Account in GTA 6
sources.text: Most of us take a bank account for granted in real life, but GTA 6 requires you to get one for Jason and Lucia. A fundamental basic for grown-ups, Jason and Lucia’s lives have made getting one difficult, but not impossible. I approached an ATM in GTA 6 ‘s early hours as Jason, and a notification popped up saying I needed a bank account. Not only that, but lots of weapons and items are locked out until you get a bank account—so let’s get one! You can buy Grand Theft Auto 6 here if you haven’t already! You get a bank account during Chapter 1, once Lucia is out of prison and reunited with Jason, and she asks Jason if they can get a bank account. In Chapter 1, the time comes for Jason to bring Lucia home. You have an evening at a bar with friends; there’s a fist fight outside, and Jason and Lucia (presumably) get quite naked with each other. However, shortly after you’re reunited, you’ll get a phone call from Lucia, asking about a bank account, and Jason replies that he hasn’t got one. As you know, Jason has a stash at his house which acts as a bank account. A main story mission sees you go to Fleeca Bank to get a bank account, and despite the bank being unable to give you a proper account, you will gain a wonderfully named BuckMe account, which you can use as an app on your phone, and it lets you finally use ATMs. BuckMe lets you deposit and withdraw money and essentially replaces the more cumbersome stash system in GTA 6. There’s a kiddish charm about having money under a floorboard, but it’s not practical for a grown adult who needs to keep thousands of dollars secure. BuckMe acts like a normal banking app, and you can also use it to increase your savings account, required to progress through the main story, as Jason and Lucia create a savings account to earn money for their child. Is it cool to see him return? Let us know your thoughts about the game via the free Insider Gaming Discord server . sources.title: Amazon Drops Lightning Deals on Some of the Best Modern Board Games for Black Friday
sources.text: You can never have too many board games. With video games and TV dominating our attention on a daily basis, there's nothing better than sitting down and having a physical experience with your family and friends. A good game of Monopoly or Scrabble is always entertaining, but if you're looking to upgrade to something a bit more modern, Black Friday sales are a great time to do so. Amazon just dropped a number of Lightning Deals on some of our favorite modern tabletop games in 2026. Amazon's Black Friday sale kicked off on November 19, so these board game deals are new to today. You can dive into our top picks right here or scroll down for some of IGN's reviews on these games. Seeing as these are Lightning Deals, we don't expext these discounts to last through the weekend. The majority of Amazon's new board game deals are from Asmodee. That's not too surprising considering they own a variety of different studios. While we haven't reviewed every board game on this list, we have played all of them and can attest to just how fun they are. If you're looking for new tabletop experiences, any of these options are an easy recommendation. You can check out some of our hands-on reviews with these games below if you want to know more about the experience. This is one of the best Lord of the Rings board games on the market right now. We gave it an 8 out of 10 score in our review : "Lord of the Rings: Fate of the Fellowship expands on the 2008's Pandemic game system and manages to create one of the best Lord of the Ring tabletop experiences out there, but its increased reliance on random card draws and dice rolls can lead to some turns feeling wasted, or that you are biding your time for what you need, detracting from the game's excitement." - Scott White If you're looking for a racing board game, look no further than this one right here. We gave this game a 9 out of 10 in our review : "Heat: Pedal to the Metal is a vivid and delightful racing board game that surpasses the accomplishments of all that came before it. It’s an inspired title in both product and design, offering a range of options while presenting a dynamic racing system that is extremely impressive." - Charlie Theel For a fun and unique family board game , Harmonies is an excellent choice. We gave it an 8 out of 10 in our review : "Harmonies masterfully blends its drafting system and token-laying mechanics to create a satisfying gameplay loop with just the right amount of tension in its decision-making. At its core, it's an elegant optimization puzzle that offers a fresh challenge every time you play. The added verticality introduces another layer of strategy as you work to build the perfect mix of habitats. Its playful, inviting design features vibrant colors and beautifully illustrated animal cards that are a joy to engage with throughout the game. It's quick to set up and easy to teach, making it a great fit for families and couples, while still offering enough crunchy decisions to keep seasoned players satisfied." - Matt Adler If you're looking for a fun strategy game with civilization elements, 7 Wonders will be right up your alley. It's not for everyone, but it's still worth picking up at this price. We gave it a 7 out of 10 in our review : "You can’t argue with the sheer number of copies that 7 Wonders has sold, nor the plethora of awards that it has accrued. This is a fun game, a good way to pass a half hour, with a great balance of luck and strategy. But it got that way by spreading itself quite thin, making a lot of gamers fairly happy rather than bringing ecstasy to smaller fanbases. There are times when the lack of theme and long-term strategy makes it feel more like an exercise than a game and it’s a tad too involved for casual family play. But whatever kind of games you like, if you fancy taking the plunge, you’re almost guaranteed to find plenty of enjoyment." - Matt Thrower Jacob Kienlen is a Senior Audience Development Strategist and Writer for IGN. stories.title: Cyberleek Returns for GTA 6 Launch to Reportedly Release a Near-Complete Xbox Build, Threatens to Release the Game's Executable in Days
stories.summary: Cyberleek has returned for the launch of GTA 6 to allegedly release a near complete Xbox build of the game — and has threatened to release its executable in just days.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Cyberleek Returns for GTA 6 Launch to Reportedly Release a Near-Complete Xbox Build, Threatens to Release the Game's Executable in Days
sources.text: Cyberleek has returned for the launch of GTA 6 to allegedly release a near complete Xbox build of the game — and has threatened to release its executable in just days. It was thought that the person or group responsible for the online Cyberleek persona had ended their spate of GTA 6 leaks last month, after their memecoin crashed despite efforts to boost its market cap. In October, Cyberleek had tied various types of GTA 6 gameplay leaks to the Cyberleek market cap, and threatened to release a build of the game — supposedly over 200 GB in size — if the memecoin hit a $30 million market cap. Gameplay clips reportedly leaked at the time allegedly showed Lucia fully naked — something that is not possible in the final launch version of the game. Yesterday, November 19 — the GTA 6 release date — Cyberleek returned to drop a GTA 6 Xbox build without the game's executable. In a statement reportedly published online , Cyberleek claimed this Xbox build is a “full November 2026 build of GTA 6.” They predicted this Xbox build would be used to emulate GTA 6 on PC “within a week, running far past 30fps.” The console version of GTA 6 targets 30fps across all platforms, although struggles at times to hit that on base PS5 and Xbox Series X and S. Cyberleek has revived their crypto scheme, promising to release the executable immediately if it hits a $15 million market cap. While the CyberLeek memecoin was boosted in value by the news to $1.9 million yesterday, it is unlikely to get anywhere near the target. Still, Cyberleek has vowed to release the final file anyway on November 23, whether the memecoin hits the market cap or not. The release of a full and recent build of GTA 6 would of course be hugely damaging for Rockstar and parent company Take-Two, which appears to have been unable to deter Cyberleek’s actions in any meaningful way since their spate of leaks began. It would also run counter to the thought that Cyberleek only had access to an early development build of GTA 6, a feeling that was reinforced not only by the videos that were released, but by the differences that have emerged following the game’s official launch. Fans are calling on people not to spend money on Cyberleek, pointing out the leaker cashed out back in August and did again in October. Analysis of cryptocurrency transactions in late August pointed to the GTA 6 leaker cashing out having earnt around $270,000. IGN had reported on fan skepticism around the alleged leaked gameplay that reportedly showed both Jason and Lucia fully naked . A previous leaked gameplay video allegedly showed a tank spawning into the world, which suggested access to a dev menu of some kind. The leaked videos allegedly showing both Jason and Lucia fully naked also show NPCs failing to react to that in any way, which suggested this effect was achieved with either a dev menu or cheats. Cyberleek had threatened Rockstar and Take-Two with the release of a full playthrough of the game’s story if they failed to release GTA 6 on-disc and issue a public apology — and the market cap of the memecoin hit $30 million. Of course, few believe these GTA 6 leaks are about campaigning for physical media — rather they're about making money from a crypto scam. Cyberleek appeared to go dark after a spate of high-profile GTA 6 leaks in August that sparked an investigation from Take-Two. The company issued subpoenas to the likes of Discord as part of the hunt for the person or group of people responsible. It remains unclear how the gameplay footage, or any potential build of the game it's taken from, escaped the confines of Rockstar's infamous tight security. In August, Rockstar addressed the GTA 6 leaks , describing the situation as "heartbreaking" for its development team and "unfortunate" for fans. At the time, the developer acknowledged that its intended experience for players "may now be impacted by some spoilers," but reiterated GTA 6's previously-confirmed launch date of November 19. Whether the culprit or culprits are ever caught may rest on how successful Take-Two's legal team and the relevant authorities are at forcing social networks or crypto exchanges to divulge any personal details they hold on those responsible. Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

stories.title: GTA 6 Players Find Red Dead Redemption Lore That Strongly Suggests Both Series Are Set in the Same Universe
stories.summary: Players have found lore in GTA 6 that strongly suggest the game takes place in the same universe as Rockstar’s Red Dead Redemption series, in a move that has excited fans about the prospect of a canon merger of timelines.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: GTA 6 Players Find Red Dead Redemption Lore That Strongly Suggests Both Series Are Set in the Same Universe
sources.text: Players have found lore in GTA 6 that strongly suggest the game takes place in the same universe as Rockstar’s Red Dead Redemption series, in a move that has excited fans about the prospect of a canon merger of timelines. Warning! Spoilers for GTA 6 and Red Dead Redemption 2 follow. We’ve already found Arthur Morgan’s hat in GTA 6, but there’s another thing connecting the two games. A readable book found in Brian’s Marina in Key Lento has multiple references to Red Dead Redemption and its sequel. X / Twitter user GameRoll shared excerpts from the book online. The book is a chronicle of the life and death of Flaco Hernandez, a gunslinger Arthur Morgan hunts to his cabin by Cairn Lake in Grizzlies West during the The Noblest of Men, and a Woman stranger mission in RDR 2. The book itself could even be the chronicle you help Theodore Levin write by hunting down the gunslingers, or at least a modern reinterpretation of it. It’s told from the viewpoint of Rust McCreary, an original character who doesn’t appear in either RDR game. In the book, he comes across the corpse of Hernandez in the snow at Cairn Lake, right where you leave him in the RDR 2 mission. According to the book, Hernandez had a bullet hole right in the center of his forehead, so it’s canon that you can actually aim good. The book also references multiple locations, from New Austin to Armadillo and Blackwater. It’s not quite confirmation that Jason is a direct descendant of Arthur Morgan or anything like that, but it’s a cool detail that basically turns RDR into a prequel to GTA 4 and its sequels. Like Dutch, Rockstar had a plan all along. Players have even found license plates for New Austin in GTA 6 . New Austin is one of the states in which Red Dead takes place, and is assumed to be Rockstar's version of Texas. It's not the first time Rockstar has connected the games. In the first iteration of GTA Online, the character creator allowed you to share genetics with John Marston, protagonist of the first RDR, to create a visual basis for your original character. Fans of the two games are generally happy with the connection. "Honestly? Good," said one X / Twitter user . "I was annoyed that technically both canons weren't linked. By linking them, it makes the universe feel bigger." "That is so cool," said another . "This GTA trully feels like RDR. And I really enjoy the calmer aproach I even try to be as good with jason to give them the better possible ending." Another social media user wasn't as convinced because of characters in older Rockstar games mentioning California and Florida, instead of their in-universe names of San Andreas and Leonida: "It’s weird though, because in Red Dead Redemption 2 they call certain states or cities by their real names, but in GTA they use fictionalized names of cities and states. So many retcons it’s painful." Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? Check out the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN. If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips and Chapter 2 Guide and Tips . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map . Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. sources.title: Your GTA 6 car is your Red Dead 2 horse, and it's perfect
sources.text: Every time the very concept of a GTA 6 has come up in the past eight years, I've had just one wistful opinion to contribute: "I hope they make it more like Red Dead Redemption 2." I'm not a huge GTA guy, but I am a Red Dead head. The sequel is Rockstar's best work (maybe second best now?) because of all the ways it prioritizes roleplay and choice-making by simulating the little things: Mixing tonics, crafting bullets individually, grooming Arthur's mustache. God, I love that stuff. There was no way Rockstar would repeat all of these life sim-y touches for the louder and faster GTA 6, but I am surprised and elated that my favorite Red Dead 2 feature of them all made the cut: Your car is your horse. That is to say, Jason and Lucia's personal vehicles are their mobile bases—an essential extension of them. You can't pet or name it, sadly, but it's important to keep track of and take care of your whip, because it's where you keep all your guns and outfits. It's all literally in the trunk: If you want to fetch your shotgun, you have to walk to the back of the car, open it up, and fish it out of a box. Gone are the days of keeping seven assault rifles, ten SMGs, and four rocket launchers in your back pocket—you can only equip two "long" guns on your back, and large melee weapons like bats have to be stowed away, too. Aside from how cool it is to fish a shotgun out of my trunk like a disgruntled Jason Statham character, the limitation is forcing me to think twice about how to approach missions. And unlike in Red Dead's lawless towns, the NPCs of Leonida seem to react negatively to the guy walking around with assault rifles on his back. The game tells you early on that police pay closer attention to you when openly carrying firearms—another reason to stow them away when you don't need 'em. The car trunk is also where extra outfits can be stored. You can bring along five by default (more than Red Dead's saddles allowed), and even this isn't just for vanity. GTA 6's wanted system goes further than police chases: if you lose the cops, your wanted level will linger and cops identify you based on your description, clothes, and your car. The easiest way to go incognito after raising cain is to pull over, pop the trunk, and change outfits. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. It's all very smart and cool and I love it. Though I can also understand why others wouldn't—it's a significant break from what GTA has been up to this point. The two gun limit means murderous rampages might end earlier than they used to, and I can foresee getting annoyed the first time I bring a sniper rifle to a shotgun fight and have no way to correct that. But I think this reflects how Rockstar designed GTA 6 to be just as much a life sim as a crime fantasy. GTA 6 wants me to constantly make choices and consider what a real human would do. Like in one mission last night, I was left alone without my personal vehicle for the first time. Instead of Rockstar suggesting I grand theft an auto, a tutorial popped for calling a cab. So yea, I took a yellow cab back to my car a few miles away, and it was a chill ride, except for the cabbie who rudely shot down my attempts to make small talk. He's lucky my guns were in my car. sources.title: GTA 6’s Official Connection to Red Dead Redemption Revealed
sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 may have just come out, but players have already discovered many of Leonida's most bizarre secrets, including the return of a certain legendary cryptid . One of these Easter eggs contains a big reveal: Red Dead Redemption and Grand Theft Auto are set in the same universe. A book found in Brian’s Marina in Key Lento contains multiple references to Red Dead Redemption and its sequel. As GameRoll reported on X, the novel describes the demise of Flaco Hernandez, whom Arthur Morgan cut down in Red Dead Redemption 2 ’s “The Noblest of Men, and a Woman” mission. The story is told from the perspective of a new character, Rust McCreary, who comes across Hernandez’s corpse at Cairn Lake, where Arthur bested him in a duel. The book also references Red Dead Redemption 2 locations like New Austin, Armadillo, and Blackwater. The book isn’t the only reference to Rockstar’s western. You can spot license plates from New Austin, Red Dead’s fictionalized version of Texas. Jason can even rock a cowboy hat that looks exactly like Arthur's. This isn’t the first time that Rockstar's franchises have crossed over. Franklin's house in Grand Theft Auto 5 contains a Red Dead book written by J. Marston. It’s hard to imagine John having time to document his exploits, but his son, Jack, may have provided an in-universe account of what went down in the first Red Dead game. The following contains major story spoilers for GTA 6. Beyond the ties to Red Dead, GTA 6 predictably includes many references to past Grand Theft Auto games. Jimmy De Santa, the son of GTA 5 protagonist Michael, makes a minor appearance . He's part of a mission where the player chooses whether to let him into a club. In Chapter 5, near the end of the game, Lucia and Jason begin working with GTA 4 protagonist Niko Bellic , who has returned to a life of crime. This isn't the first time GTA games have crossed over. GTA 5 infamously included a scene where Trevor killed Johnny Klebitz, the protagonist of GTA 4: The Lost and the Damned. At least Niko seems to fare much better.

sources.title: GTA 6 won't let you use cheats until you complete the main story, and locks progression when you do
sources.text: Here's a twist: you can't use cheats in Grand Theft Auto 6 until you complete the entire game's main story. That's what we discovered from our tests at least, after loading in saves at various points through the game to be sure, and it's also both a first for the series and a departure even from how developer Rockstar handled cheats in Red Dead Redemption 2 . In that game,approximately half of the cheats were available from the off, and the other half required discovering specific newspapers from around the game's world to unlock. In GTA 6, you'll again need to do some legwork. This time it appears that all of the game's cheats not only require you to finish the story, but also complete various tasks or challenges to unlock them. The way it works is simple enough. Once you finish the main story, the "Cheats" tab - previously hidden - quietly appears at the far end of the Progress menu, accessible when you open the in-game map and scroll with the bumper buttons. From there, you can view various sub-sections of cheats, sorted by category, and a list of 10 or so cheats for each. With each cheat there'll be a short explanation of what it does, and what's required to unlock it and, once unlocked, guidance on how to perform it. This is done via whipping out your phone, holding down the shoulder buttons and using various D-Pad inputs - much the same as GTA 5 . There's also another caveat to bear in mind: when you use a cheat, you'll see a notification warning you that the game can't be saved while it's active, and that Trophies and Achievements are also disabled until you end that session. This makes sense, once you understand the nature of GTA 6's story - there is a cheat for giving yourself a load of money, for instance; another departure from GTA 5 where that popular cheat was removed - but given you'll need certain amounts of cash at various points of the story, enabling you to shortcut that would disrupt the way the narrative unfolds. We'll have a guide from yours truly to all the game's cheats live on Eurogamer in the very near future, as the game releases here in the UK. In the meantime, if you find yourself on the fence about this one, be sure to give our GTA 6 review a look. As I put it there, giving the game five stars: it is "the most believable and unbelievable video game world ever made".

sources.title: How to fix the railing in GTA 6
sources.text: Complete Jason's house repairs before Lucia arrives. One of the last tasks in GTA 6 's home repair mission for Jason is to fix the railing. These tasks are important if you want Lucia to have a positive welcome when she gets out of jail, so they're well worth doing if you plan to foster a romance between the two criminal lovers. You have to fix the rooftiles, put up the panels in Jason's bedroom and paint them, repair the stairs up to the decking at the front, and finally, fix the railing. This one is slightly less obvious, but you just need to: You can also just watch the clip above if unsure. The other tasks are relatively simple if you haven't found them yet also. Climb the ladder outside the front door to repair the roof tiles, interact with the stacked panels at the foot of Jason's bed to put them up, and you can repair the stairs at the front by interacting with the pile of planks at the bottom.
